findings.text: Pressing Refine twice does not refresh the same stages, which is what the doc comment promises: `AISessionConversation.js:172` builds the prompt id from `Number(at)`, but `at` is the transcript's ISO `timestamp` string (`AISessionConversation.read`), so `Number()` gives NaN and every press falls back to `Date.now()`, making a new id and a new copy of the stages. Use `Date.parse(at)` instead.

Long prompts fail by design: `/api/refine` accepts 64 kB of JSON, and a bubble that joins many pieces (`Chat.js:256`) goes over the 20k-character limit STATE mentions. The proof only passed after `TRUNC=1` cut the text to 300 characters (`button-proof.mjs:69`), so the real button was never shown working on a full long prompt. The error does appear on the button, but trimming the text, or saying on the button that it is too long, would be kinder.

`ThingsStage.views` (`ThingsStage.js:377`, filled in `render()`) only ever grows: every stage view drawn on a page stays referenced after it is gone. This is small, but a `loading.then(() => this.draw())` inside `render()` would do the same job without the Set.

`ThingsStage` matches against `maps["#"]` once, when `things.json` loads (`ThingsStage.js:380`). A `#` name registered after that will not be matched until the page reloads. This is fine if the Mention maps are filled at import time, which they appear to be.
`VoiceStage.js:8` still says "The five: RawStage → … CardsStage" in its doc comment. The readme and `voice-to-page.md` were updated to six stages; this comment was missed.
The proofs and `STATE.md` are only in the diff; this review had no screenshots, so it checks the code only (no widths given). `things-proof-*.png` exist for 400/1200/1920/3440 in the diff.

answer.reply: noted: long prompts hit the 20k limit; the error shows on the button; trimming is the next step in STATE
noted: the views Set is tiny, kept
noted: Mention maps fill at import time, before things.json resolves
fixed: VoiceStage.js doc says six stages
noted: proofs are committed in the worktree

The reason given for not building the Opus voice overseer misquotes the owner. asks.md #10 says "the owner said Haiku never runs the show", but that quote is about Haiku, not Opus (content: say what you mean).

Each "Things you mentioned" link is a full-width black bar. At 1920 a one-word name (`Dictate`) stretches about 900 px, so five bars outweigh the words you said (things-proof-1920.png, top prompt, right column).
The importance and confidence bars carry no number; the value is in a hover `title` only. The 0.75em grey labels are faint (cards-meters.png).
